symbols.name: \(p\)
symbols.def: Dimension of the reduced-form Gaussian shift.

symbols.name: \(\lambda^p\)
symbols.def: The \(p\)-dimensional Lebesgue measure.

symbols.name: \(n\)
symbols.def: Index of the original local experiment.

symbols.name: \(\nu\)
symbols.def: Index of a sequence of nearby endpoint games.

symbols.name: \(a\)
symbols.def: Generic binary treatment level.

symbols.name: \(Y(a)\)
symbols.def: Potential outcome under treatment level \(a\).

symbols.name: \(J_{-}\)
symbols.def: Finite index set for affine pieces of the lower endpoint.

symbols.name: \(J_{+}\)
symbols.def: Finite index set for affine pieces of the upper endpoint.

symbols.name: \(j\)
symbols.def: Generic lower-endpoint face index.

symbols.name: \(k\)
symbols.def: Generic upper-endpoint face index.

symbols.name: \(H\)
symbols.def: Compact convex polytope of Gaussian means.

symbols.name: \(h\)
symbols.def: Generic reduced-form mean in the endpoint game.

symbols.name: \(h_0\)
symbols.def: A reduced-form mean at which the welfare interval straddles zero.

symbols.name: \(m\)
symbols.def: Index of a restricted endpoint-state game.

symbols.name: \(\Sigma\)
symbols.def: Known positive-definite covariance matrix.

symbols.name: \(a_j^{-}\)
symbols.def: Intercept of lower affine piece \(j\).

symbols.name: \(b_j^{-}\)
symbols.def: Slope vector of lower affine piece \(j\).

symbols.name: \(a_k^{+}\)
symbols.def: Intercept of upper affine piece \(k\).

symbols.name: \(b_k^{+}\)
symbols.def: Slope vector of upper affine piece \(k\).

symbols.name: \(U^{\ast}\)
symbols.def: Population welfare gain from assigning the target population to treatment rather than control.

symbols.name: \(\varphi_{\Sigma}\)
symbols.def: Density of \(N(0,\Sigma)\) with respect to Lebesgue measure.

symbols.name: \(Z_h\)
symbols.def: \(Z_h\sim N(h,\Sigma)\) for \(h\in H\).

symbols.name: \(E_h\)
symbols.def: Expectation under the law of \(Z_h\).

symbols.name: \(\delta\)
symbols.def: Generic Lebesgue-almost-everywhere equivalence class of Borel-measurable treatment probabilities; pointwise notation uses an arbitrary Borel representative.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal D\)
symbols.space: the positive order interval in the closed unit ball of \(L^{\infty}(\lambda^p)\), with the weak-star topology \(\sigma(L^{\infty}(\lambda^p),L^1(\lambda^p))\)
symbols.def: Weak-star compact rule class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:rule-class}\), whose elements are \(\lambda^p\)-almost-everywhere equivalence classes.

symbols.name: \(\delta^{\star}\)
symbols.def: Generic minimizer of worst-case endpoint regret.

symbols.name: \(q_{\delta}\)
symbols.def: \(q_{\delta}(h)=E_h[\delta(Z_h)]\).

symbols.name: \(s\)
symbols.def: Generic pair \(s=(h,\sigma_s)\) with endpoint sign \(\sigma_s\in\{+,-\}\).

symbols.name: \(R\)
symbols.def: \(R(\delta)=\sup_{s\in S}r_s(\delta)\).

symbols.name: \(v\)
symbols.def: \(v=\inf_{\delta\in\mathcal D}R(\delta)\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi\)
symbols.def: Nature's mixed-strategy space endowed with weak convergence.

symbols.name: \(\pi\)
symbols.def: Generic probability measure on signed endpoint states.

symbols.name: \(A_{\pi,+}\)
symbols.def: \(A_{\pi,+}(z)=\int_H c_{+}(h)\varphi_{\Sigma}(z-h)\,d\pi(h,+)\).

symbols.name: \(A_{\pi,-}\)
symbols.def: \(A_{\pi,-}(z)=\int_H c_{-}(h)\varphi_{\Sigma}(z-h)\,d\pi(h,-)\).

symbols.name: \(b\)
symbols.def: \(b(\pi)=\int_{\mathbb R^p}\min\{A_{\pi,+}(z),A_{\pi,-}(z)\}\,dz\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal D^{\star}\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D^{\star}=\{\delta\in\mathcal D:R(\delta)=v\}\).

symbols.name: \(\Pi^{\star}\)
symbols.def: \(\Pi^{\star}=\{\pi\in\Pi:b(\pi)=v\}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathfrak F^{\star}\)
symbols.def: Faces whose relative interior receives positive mass under at least one prior in \(\Pi^{\star}\), with the matching endpoint sign.

symbols.name: \(\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\)
symbols.def: Priors in \(\Pi^{\star}\) assigning positive mass to the relative interior of every face in \(\mathfrak F^{\star}\), with the matching endpoint sign.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal D_{1}\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal D_1=\{\delta\in\mathcal D:\exists w\in\mathbb R^p\setminus\{0\},\exists g:\mathbb R\to[0,1]\text{ Borel},\ \delta(z)=g(w^{\top}z)\text{ a.e.}\}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{all}}\)
symbols.def: Event \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal D^{\star}\subseteq\mathcal D_1\).

symbols.name: \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{co}}\)
symbols.def: Event \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal D^{\star}\setminus\mathcal D_1\ne\varnothing\).

symbols.name: \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{none}}\)
symbols.def: Event \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1=\varnothing\).

symbols.name: \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{idx}}\)
symbols.def: Handle constructed in \(\mathrm{def:indexability-handle}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{noidx}}\)
symbols.def: Handle constructed in \(\mathrm{def:no-index-witness-handle}\) for a finite rational prior, its Gaussian-mixture Bayes rule, and an interval-arithmetic certificate of exact saddle closure and a curved decision boundary.

symbols.name: \(S_m\)
symbols.def: Nested meshes with dense union in \(S\).

symbols.name: \(\pi_m\)
symbols.def: Dual component of the restricted-game saddle at iteration \(m\).

symbols.name: \(\delta_m\)
symbols.def: Primal component of the restricted-game saddle at iteration \(m\).

symbols.name: \(U_m\)
symbols.def: \(U_m=R(\delta_m)\).

symbols.name: \(\ell_0\)
symbols.def: \(\ell_0(h)=-4/3+\lVert h\rVert_{\infty}\).

symbols.name: \(u_0\)
symbols.def: \(u_0(h)=4/3-\lVert h\rVert_{\infty}\).

symbols.name: \(\eta\)
symbols.def: Amplitude of the bounded non-ridge perturbation.

symbols.name: \(\delta_{\eta}\)
symbols.def: \(\delta_{\eta}(z)=1/2+\eta\tanh(z_1)\tanh(z_2)\).

symbols.name: \(\mathsf G\)
symbols.def: Tuple of \(H,\Sigma,\ell,u\) and the induced game objects.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal G_p\)
symbols.space: sets of polyhedral Gaussian endpoint games
symbols.def: Class constructed in \(\mathrm{def:game-class}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal G_p^{\mathrm{cs}}\)
symbols.def: Centrosymmetric members of the compact polyhedral game class, constructed in \(\mathrm{def:centrosymmetric-comparator-class}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal O_p^{(4)}\)
symbols.def: Compact finite-faced Gaussian endpoint games that are simultaneously members of \(\mathcal G_p^{\mathrm{cs}}\) and images of models satisfying Assumption 5 under the limit-game construction of Theorem 4 in \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local}; constructed in \(\mathrm{def:theorem4-overlap}\).

symbols.name: \(d_{\mathsf G}\)
symbols.def: Maximum of the operator-norm covariance distance and the Hausdorff distances between the domains and the graphs of their lower and upper endpoint functions.

symbols.name: \(\kappa\)
symbols.def: Common numerical bound on domain radius, covariance conditioning, endpoint-face count, intercept magnitudes, and face-normal norms in the stability theorem.

symbols.name: \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}\)
symbols.def: \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\mathsf G')\) holds when the mean domain of \(\mathsf G'\) is contained in the Euclidean ball of radius \(\kappa\), every covariance eigenvalue lies in \([\kappa^{-1},\kappa]\), and every lower or upper endpoint has at most \(\kappa\) affine pieces whose intercept magnitudes and normal norms are at most \(\kappa\).

symbols.name: \(\omega_{p,\kappa}\)
symbols.def: \(\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho)=\rho\left[1+\kappa(1+\kappa)\sqrt{p\kappa^2/2+\kappa/4}\right]\).

symbols.name: \(M_{\kappa}\)
symbols.def: \(M_{\kappa}=\kappa(1+\kappa)\), an upper bound for both endpoint loss weights on the \(\kappa\)-bounded primitive collection.

symbols.name: \(\overline\omega_{p,\kappa}\)
symbols.def: \(\overline\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho)=\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho)\) for \(0\le\rho\le(2\kappa)^{-1}\), and \(\overline\omega_{p,\kappa}(\rho)=M_{\kappa}\) otherwise.

symbols.name: \(\mathsf G_{\nu}\)
symbols.def: Generic sequence converging to \(\mathsf G\) in \(d_{\mathsf G}\).

symbols.name: \(\rho_{\nu}\)
symbols.def: \(\rho_{\nu}=d_{\mathsf G}(\mathsf G_{\nu},\mathsf G)\).

symbols.name: \(v_{\nu}\)
symbols.def: Minimax-regret value of \(\mathsf G_{\nu}\).

symbols.name: \(R_{\nu}\)
symbols.def: Worst-case regret functional induced by \(\mathsf G_{\nu}\).

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon_{\nu}\)
symbols.def: Nonnegative approximation tolerance satisfying \(\varepsilon_{\nu}\to0\).

symbols.name: \(\varepsilon_n\)
symbols.def: Nonnegative stopping tolerance used for the estimated game, with \(\varepsilon_n\to0\).

symbols.name: \(\widetilde\delta_{\nu}\)
symbols.def: Rule whose certified primal-dual gap for \(\mathsf G_{\nu}\) is at most \(\varepsilon_{\nu}\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal X_n\)
symbols.def: Standard Borel sample space supporting the local experiment at index \(n\).

symbols.name: \(P_{n,h}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on \(\mathcal X_n\) indexed by \(n\) and \(h\in H\)
symbols.def: Original sampling experiment along local parameter \(h\).

symbols.name: \(T_n\)
symbols.def: Measurable statistic used in the sufficient construction for two-sided experiment equivalence.

symbols.name: \(\mathsf R_n\)
symbols.def: An \(h\)-independent Markov kernel used to reconstruct the original observation from the Gaussian-pivot statistic.

symbols.name: \(a_n\)
symbols.def: Deterministic total-variation error bound for the Gaussian-pivot approximation, with \(a_n\to0\).

symbols.name: \(b_n\)
symbols.def: Deterministic total-variation error bound for asymptotic reconstruction, with \(b_n\to0\).

symbols.name: \(K_n\)
symbols.def: Markov kernel that maps the original experiment into its Gaussian-shift approximation.

symbols.name: \(L_n\)
symbols.def: Markov kernel that maps the Gaussian-shift experiment back into an approximation of the original local experiment.

symbols.name: \(\lambda_n\)
symbols.def: \(\lambda_n=\max\{\sup_{h\in H}\lVert K_nP_{n,h}-N(h,\Sigma)\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}},\sup_{h\in H}\lVert L_nN(h,\Sigma)-P_{n,h}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\}\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat Z_n\)
symbols.def: Output drawn from \(K_n\) conditionally on the original data.

symbols.name: \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\)
symbols.def: Plug-in game built from estimated covariance and endpoint coefficients.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\Sigma_n\)
symbols.def: Covariance component of the estimated game \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\).

symbols.name: \(Q_{n,h}\)
symbols.space: probability laws on a Gaussian signal and an estimated game
symbols.def: The law obtained by first drawing \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\) from its \(P_{n,h}\)-marginal and then, conditionally on that game, drawing the signal from \(N(h,\widehat\Sigma_n)\); in particular, \(\mathcal L_{Q_{n,h}}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)=\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)\).

symbols.name: \(\gamma_n\)
symbols.def: \(\gamma_n=\sup_{h\in H}\lVert\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(\widehat Z_n,\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)-Q_{n,h}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\).

symbols.name: \(\alpha_n\)
symbols.def: \(\alpha_n=\sup_{h\in H}E_{P_{n,h}}[\overline\omega_{p,\kappa}(d_{\mathsf G}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n,\mathsf G))]\).

symbols.name: \(\widehat\delta_n\)
symbols.def: Certified near-saddle rule for \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\) evaluated at \(\widehat Z_n\).

symbols.name: \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(d)=\sup_{h\in H}\max\{c_+(h)[1-E_{P_{n,h}}d],c_-(h)E_{P_{n,h}}d\}\).

assumptions.condition: The set \(H\subset\mathbb R^p\) is a nonempty compact convex polytope with nonempty relative interior in its affine hull.
The covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) is positive definite and does not depend on \(h\).
For every \(h\in H\), the endpoints satisfy \(\ell(h)\le u(h)\).

novel.justification: This is a weaker pointwise sign-ambiguity condition, not the open-set condition in Definition 2 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision}. It is realistic when one economically plausible local reduced-form mean has strictly two-sided welfare bounds, including finite-support moment-inequality models with continuous polyhedral endpoint maps; no ambient open set of such means is required.

assumptions.condition: There exist Markov kernels \(K_n\) and \(L_n\) such that \(\lambda_n=\max\{\sup_{h\in H}\lVert K_nP_{n,h}-N(h,\Sigma)\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}},\sup_{h\in H}\lVert L_nN(h,\Sigma)-P_{n,h}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\}\to0\).

novel.justification: This is an explicit nonstandard high-level premise. Differentiability in quadratic mean or pointwise local asymptotic normality does not imply the displayed compact-\(H\), two-sided total-variation deficiency bound, so feasible transfer is conditional on this stronger equivalence. A self-contained sufficient construction is available on the standard Borel spaces \(\mathcal X_n\): suppose there are a measurable statistic \(T_n\), an \(h\)-independent reconstruction Markov kernel \(\mathsf R_n(\cdot\mid z)\), and deterministic \(a_n,b_n\to0\) such that \[\sup_{h\in H}\left\lVert\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(T_n)-N(h,\Sigma)\right\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le a_n\] and \[\sup_{h\in H}\left\lVert P_{n,h}-\int \mathsf R_n(\cdot\mid z)\,\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(T_n)(dz)\right\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\le b_n.\] Taking \(K_n(x,\cdot)=\delta_{T_n(x)}\) and \(L_n=\mathsf R_n\), contraction of total variation under \(\mathsf R_n\) and the triangle inequality give \(\lambda_n\le a_n+b_n\to0\). These conditions are uniform Gaussian-pivot approximation plus uniform asymptotic sufficiency and reconstruction; they are not claimed for every regular model and impose no convergence rate.

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\) and \(h\in H\), \(P_{n,h}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\in\mathcal G_p)=1\).

novel.justification: A training-sample construction can enforce legal membership by fitting the endpoint coefficients subject to the nonempty-interval and pointwise sign-ambiguity restrictions while maintaining a positive-definite covariance estimate. This is an independent legality requirement: numerical bounds on fitted coefficients do not imply membership in \(\mathcal G_p\).

assumptions.condition: For every \(n\) and \(h\in H\), \(P_{n,h}(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n))=1\).

novel.justification: Bounded parameterizations of compact polyhedral endpoint models and covariance estimators with eigenvalues constrained to a fixed compact interval satisfy this condition. It controls the loss envelope and continuity modulus but is separate from legal membership in \(\mathcal G_p\).

assumptions.condition: The joint approximation error satisfies \(\gamma_n=\sup_{h\in H}\lVert\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(\widehat Z_n,\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)-Q_{n,h}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0\).

novel.justification: A concrete sufficient construction uses a training split to form \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\), including \(\widehat\Sigma_n\), with legal membership and the numerical bounds imposed separately by \(\mathrm{ass:estimated-game-legality}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:estimated-game-kappa-bounds}\), and a conditionally independent evaluation split to form \(\widehat Z_n\). If the conditional Gaussian approximation obeys \[\sup_{h\in H}E_{P_{n,h}}\!\left[\left\lVert\mathcal L_{P_{n,h}}(\widehat Z_n\mid\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)-N(h,\widehat\Sigma_n)\right\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\right]\to0,\] then the common \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\)-marginal and conditional disintegration give \(\gamma_n\) no larger than the displayed quantity, hence \(\gamma_n\to0\). This sample-splitting or stable-construction requirement is independent of the two-sided experiment equivalence in \(\mathrm{ass:uniform-two-sided-experiment-equivalence}\), and neither joint approximation nor numerical boundedness substitutes for legal membership in \(\mathcal G_p\).

definitions.name: Compact polyhedral Gaussian endpoint games \(\mathcal G_p\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_p=\{\mathsf G=(H,\Sigma,\ell,u):\mathsf G\text{ satisfies }\mathrm{ass:compact-polyhedral-domain},\mathrm{ass:nondegenerate-gaussian-shift},\mathrm{ass:nonempty-identified-interval},\mathrm{ass:nontrivial-sign-ambiguity}\}\), where \(\ell(h)=\max_{j\in J_-}\{a_j^-+(b_j^-)^{\top}h\}\) and \(u(h)=\min_{k\in J_+}\{a_k^++(b_k^+)^{\top}h\}\).

definitions.name: Compact centered polyhedral subclass \(\mathcal G_p^{\mathrm{cs}}\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal G_p^{\mathrm{cs}}=\{\mathsf G=(H,\Sigma,\ell,u)\in\mathcal G_p:H=-H\text{ and }u(h)=-\ell(-h)\text{ for every }h\in H\}\).

definitions.name: Exact compact-polyhedral overlap with Theorem 4
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal O_p^{(4)}=\{\mathsf G=(H,\Sigma,\ell,u)\in\mathcal G_p^{\mathrm{cs}}:(H,\Sigma,\ell,u)\text{ is exactly the Gaussian mean domain, covariance, and pair of lower and upper directional-derivative endpoint maps entering the cited Theorem 4}\}\). The cited result is Theorem 4 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local}.

definitions.name: Unrestricted randomized decision space \(\mathcal D\)
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal D=\{\delta\in L^{\infty}(\lambda^p):0\le\delta\le1\ \lambda^p\text{-almost everywhere}\}\), the positive order interval in the closed unit ball, equipped with \(\sigma(L^{\infty}(\lambda^p),L^1(\lambda^p))\). Its elements are \(\lambda^p\)-almost-everywhere equivalence classes. Whenever \(\delta(z)\) is written, an arbitrary Borel representative is used; because every \(N(h,\Sigma)\) is equivalent to \(\lambda^p\), \(q_{\delta}\), every regret, and every Bayes response are representative-invariant.

definitions.name: Endpoint minimax game
definitions.construction: For \(s=(h,+)\), set \(r_s(\delta)=c_+(h)\{1-q_{\delta}(h)\}\); for \(s=(h,-)\), set \(r_s(\delta)=c_-(h)q_{\delta}(h)\); then \(R(\delta)=\sup_{s\in S}r_s(\delta)\) and \(v=\inf_{\delta\in\mathcal D}R(\delta)\).

definitions.name: Gaussian-mixture Bayes envelope
definitions.construction: For \(\pi\in\Pi\), form \(A_{\pi,+}\), \(A_{\pi,-}\), and \(B_{\pi}=A_{\pi,+}-A_{\pi,-}\); the dual payoff is \(b(\pi)=\int_{\mathbb R^p}\min\{A_{\pi,+}(z),A_{\pi,-}(z)\}\,dz\), and its Bayes responses are exactly the rules with \(\delta(z)=1\) on \(\{B_{\pi}>0\}\), \(\delta(z)=0\) on \(\{B_{\pi}<0\}\), and arbitrary values in \([0,1]\) on \(\{B_{\pi}=0\}\).

definitions.name: Primal and dual optimal correspondences
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal D^{\star}=\{\delta\in\mathcal D:R(\delta)=v\}\) and \(\Pi^{\star}=\{\pi\in\Pi:b(\pi)=v\}\); a pair \((\delta,\pi)\) is a saddle when \(\int r_s(\delta)\,d\pi'(s)\le\int r_s(\delta)\,d\pi(s)\le\int r_s(\delta')\,d\pi(s)\) for every \(\delta'\in\mathcal D\) and \(\pi'\in\Pi\).

definitions.name: Face-complete dual representative
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak F^{\star}\) is the finite collection of lower or upper endpoint faces whose relative interior receives positive mass under some \(\pi\in\Pi^{\star}\); \(\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\) consists of the priors in \(\Pi^{\star}\) placing positive mass on the relative interior of every member of \(\mathfrak F^{\star}\) with its endpoint sign.

definitions.name: Full-correspondence indexability trichotomy
definitions.construction: The game lies in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{all}}\) when \(\varnothing\ne\mathcal D^{\star}\subseteq\mathcal D_1\), in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{co}}\) when both \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1\) and \(\mathcal D^{\star}\setminus\mathcal D_1\) are nonempty, and in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{none}}\) when \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Normal-fan and Gaussian-score classification handle \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{idx}}\)
definitions.construction: Derive a finite certificate from the covariance-whitened endpoint-face normals, the incidence pattern of faces hit by \(\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\), ridge factorization of the Gaussian-mixture scores \(B_{\pi}\), and the annihilator space of bounded perturbations that preserve every binding convolution moment; use it to decide \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{all}}\), \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{co}}\), or \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{none}}\).

definitions.name: Finite rational and interval-arithmetic witness handle \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{noidx}}\)
definitions.construction: Search over games whose vertices of \(H\), entries of \(\Sigma\), endpoint intercepts, and endpoint normals are rational, and over finite endpoint priors \(\pi\) with rational support points, rational masses, and unequal total masses on the two endpoint signs. Use the Gaussian-mixture Bayes rule \(\delta(z)=\mathbf 1\{B_{\pi}(z)>0\}\). Certify exact saddle closure by a rational number \(q\), a finite rational box partition of \(H\), a finite rational truncation box in \(\mathbb R^2\), outward-rounded interval enclosures, and analytic Gaussian-tail bounds proving \(R(\delta)\le q\le b(\pi)\). Certify a genuinely curved boundary on a rational box meeting \(\{B_{\pi}=0\}\) by interval lower bounds away from zero for the score gradient and the signed curvature numerator of that level set.

definitions.name: Unrestricted primal-dual exchange certificate
definitions.construction: Fix a dense sequence in \(S\) and start from a finite \(S_1\subset S\). At iteration \(m\), solve the restricted game against \(S_m\) over all \(\delta\in\mathcal D\), choose a restricted saddle \((\delta_m,\pi_m)\), compute \(L_m=b(\pi_m)\) and \(U_m=R(\delta_m)\), and adjoin both the next point of the dense sequence and an endpoint state attaining \(U_m\); stop only when \(G_m=U_m-L_m\) is below the requested tolerance.

definitions.name: Tie-uniform certified selector

statements.statement: For every \(\delta\in\mathcal D\) and \(h\in H\), the supremum of expected regret over \(U^{\ast}\in[\ell(h),u(h)]\) equals \(\max\{c_+(h)[1-q_{\delta}(h)],c_-(h)q_{\delta}(h)\}\). Consequently, Nature loses no value by restricting its pure strategies to \(S=H\times\{+,-\}\).
statements.justification: The reduction identifies the exact adversarial state space and prevents a hidden restriction to hand-picked endpoint pairs.
statements.gap: MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local writes the interval game directly; the present lemma isolates the signed endpoint game needed for unrestricted duality.
statements.consumer: Every saddle certificate and every numerical separation oracle operates on the reduced endpoint-state space.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathsf G\in\mathcal G_p\), minimax equality and attainment hold: \[v=\min_{\delta\in\mathcal D}\max_{s\in S}r_s(\delta)=\max_{\pi\in\Pi}b(\pi).\] The sets \(\mathcal D^{\star}\) and \(\Pi^{\star}\) are nonempty and convex. A pair \((\delta,\pi)\in\mathcal D\times\Pi\) is a saddle if and only if: first, \(\delta\) has the Bayes-response form determined by the sign of \(B_{\pi}\); second, \(r_s(\delta)\le v\) for every \(s\in S\); and third, \(r_s(\delta)=v\) for \(\pi\)-almost every \(s\). The set \(\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\) is nonempty. Indeed, if \(\mathfrak F^{\star}\ne\varnothing\), choose for each \(F\in\mathfrak F^{\star}\) a prior \(\pi_F\in\Pi^{\star}\) assigning positive mass to the relative interior of \(F\) with its endpoint sign; the finite uniform convex combination of the \(\pi_F\) belongs to the convex set \(\Pi^{\star}\) and lies in \(\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\). If \(\mathfrak F^{\star}=\varnothing\), every prior in the nonempty set \(\Pi^{\star}\) is face-complete. Finally, every \(\delta\in\mathcal D^{\star}\) forms a saddle with every \(\pi\in\Pi^{\star}\).
statements.justification: This is the theorem-level kernel: it gives the value, existence, every saddle, and a face-complete dual representative over all measurable randomized rules in the asymmetric polyhedral regime.
statements.gap: Yata2025Optimal uses an antipodal modulus pair under centrosymmetry. Assumption 5(i) and Theorem 4 of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local supply selected rules for a directionally differentiable limit game under convexity and centrosymmetry. The compact asymmetric polyhedral regime is an orthogonal case left open by that source, and the present theorem does not claim to contain its full Assumption-5 class.
statements.consumer: An applied researcher can certify a treatment rule without assuming it is a threshold or selecting one optimizer from a potentially large correspondence.

statements.statement: For the exchange construction in \(\mathrm{def:exchange-certificate}\), \(L_m\le v\le U_m\) at every iteration, \(L_m\uparrow v\), and \(G_m\to0\). Every weak limit point of \(\pi_m\) lies in \(\Pi^{\star}\). Regard each \(\delta_m\) as its \(\lambda^p\)-almost-everywhere equivalence class in \(\mathcal D\subset L^{\infty}(\lambda^p)\); every cluster point in the weak-star topology \(\sigma(L^{\infty}(\lambda^p),L^1(\lambda^p))\) along a subsequence with \(G_m\to0\) lies in \(\mathcal D^{\star}\). These conclusions make no iteration-complexity or convergence-rate claim.
statements.justification: The proposition turns the analytic saddle theorem into checkable global upper and lower certificates and places selector convergence in the weak-star compact topology of the unrestricted \(L^{\infty}\) rule space.
statements.gap: AradillasFernandezEtAl2025Epsilon certifies mixtures over a fixed finite rule menu; the changed first step here generates Bayes rules and violated endpoint states while preserving the measurable-rule envelope.
statements.consumer: The certificate supplies a stopping diagnostic for robust treatment-choice implementations and produces candidate least-favorable priors for analytic study.

statements.justification: This isolates the algebraic certificate implication from the substantive continuity and experiment-transfer arguments.
statements.gap: The inequality is weak-duality bookkeeping rather than a new stability theorem; stating it separately prevents the transfer claim from receiving novelty credit for an immediate step.
statements.consumer: Every finite stopping tolerance becomes an auditable excess-regret bound before any perturbation or LAN approximation is invoked.

statements.statement: The construction in \(\mathrm{def:coexistence-witness}\) is a legal member of \(\mathcal G_2\) but not of \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\), because \(H_0\ne-H_0\). Its minimax value is \(v=2/3\). The constant rule \(\delta_0\) belongs to \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1\). For every \(0<\eta\le1/2\), the rule \(\delta_{\eta}\) belongs to \(\mathcal D^{\star}\setminus\mathcal D_1\). Therefore \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\subsetneq\mathcal G_2\), and the witness game lies in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{co}}\).
statements.justification: This proposition verifies the presolve value, proves the strict internal inclusion \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\subsetneq\mathcal G_2\), and shows why existence of one optimal index rule cannot classify the full correspondence.
statements.gap: Assumption 5(i) and Theorem 4 of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local address a directionally differentiable regime under centrosymmetry, while MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision constructs multiple one-index optima in a centrosymmetric setting; neither supplies this asymmetric triangular game with simultaneous one-index and genuinely non-one-index optima.
statements.consumer: The witness is the mandatory regression test for any claimed general indexability criterion and for software that reports a single optimal rule.

statements.statement: The actual compact-polyhedral overlap with Theorem 4 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local} is a proper subclass of the proposed two-dimensional regime: \[\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\subsetneq\mathcal G_2.\] The inclusion follows from \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\subseteq\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\subseteq\mathcal G_2\), while strictness is certified by the triangular game in \(\mathrm{prop:coexistence-witness}\), which belongs to \(\mathcal G_2\) but not to \(\mathcal G_2^{\mathrm{cs}}\), and hence not to \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\). Thus \(\mathrm{thm:complete-saddle-duality}\) applies both to every game in the compact-polyhedral overlap and to at least one asymmetric game outside that overlap. Separately, for every \(\mathsf G\in\mathcal G_p^{\mathrm{cs}}\) whose modulus extremizer generates an antipodal least-favorable pair, that two-point prior and its Bayes rule satisfy the saddle conditions in \(\mathrm{thm:complete-saddle-duality}\), so the resulting rule and value agree with the compact-polyhedral specialization of Yata2025Optimal. No inclusion between \(\mathcal G_p\) and the full published Assumption-5 class is asserted.
statements.justification: The proposition proves the only strict-extension statement used in the proposal: the new two-dimensional class strictly contains the actual compact-polyhedral Theorem 4 overlap, with strictness supplied by an explicit asymmetric game.
statements.gap: Assumption 5 with Theorem 4 of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local covers a directionally differentiable centrosymmetric class, and Yata2025Optimal gives the antipodal centered benchmark. This proposition compares only on the defined compact-polyhedral overlap and does not claim that the proposed class contains the full published Assumption-5 class.
statements.consumer: Researchers can identify exactly when the published centered solver is recovered and when the asymmetric all-saddle analysis supplies genuinely additional admissible games.

statements.statement: Can \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{idx}}\) be completed into a finite, non-tautological necessary-and-sufficient criterion, stated only in the covariance-whitened endpoint-face normals, face incidence, and supports of face-complete least-favorable priors, that decides whether a game in \(\mathcal G_p\) lies in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{all}}\), \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{co}}\), or \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{none}}\)? The criterion must separately certify ridge factorization of every forced Bayes response and the presence or absence of non-ridge perturbations preserving all binding risks.
statements.justification: This exposes the non-tautological geometric classification as the central open content rather than confusing an exhibited index rule with factorization of all optima.
statements.gap: MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision proves multiplicity and excludes some threshold rules, while Yata2025Optimal exhibits one optimal index under symmetry; neither classifies the unrestricted optimal correspondence.
statements.consumer: A policy maker can learn whether reporting one scalar score is lossless, merely one admissible representation, or impossible for every minimax rule.

statements.statement: Does there exist a game in \(\mathcal G_p\) with \(p=2\), rational vertices of \(H\), rational entries of \(\Sigma\), rational endpoint intercepts and normals, and a finite prior \(\pi\in\Pi^{\mathrm{fc}}\) having rational support points, rational masses, and unequal total masses on the two endpoint signs, such that its Gaussian-mixture Bayes rule \(\delta(z)=\mathbf 1\{B_{\pi}(z)>0\}\) satisfies the exact equality \(R(\delta)=b(\pi)\), the zero set of \(B_{\pi}\) contains a smooth arc with nonzero curvature, and the game lies in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{none}}\); or are these requirements impossible in two dimensions? An affirmative certificate must instantiate \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{noidx}}\): give a rational \(q\), finite rational box partitions, outward-rounded interval enclosures, and analytic Gaussian-tail bounds proving \(R(\delta)\le q\le b(\pi)\), which yields \(R(\delta)=b(\pi)=v=q\) by weak duality. It must also enclose \(B_{\pi}\), its first two derivatives, and the signed curvature numerator on a rational box meeting \(\{B_{\pi}=0\}\), with a strictly positive rational lower bound on the gradient norm and on the absolute curvature numerator; certify \(B_{\pi}\not\equiv0\), so the Bayes rule is unique almost everywhere; and use the curved arc plus the all-saddle characterization to prove \(\mathcal D^{\star}\cap\mathcal D_1=\varnothing\).
statements.justification: This is the early kill test for the no-one-index branch and demands finite rational data, exact primal-dual closure, and a reproducible interval-arithmetic curvature certificate rather than a numerical plot.
statements.gap: Tetenov2012Asymmetric retains threshold structure in point-identified asymmetric problems, and the known partial-identification examples do not certify an unbalanced globally minimax non-halfspace rule.
statements.consumer: A certified example would establish that multivariate reporting is sometimes intrinsically necessary; an impossibility theorem would sharply simplify the classification program.

statements.justification: The explicit primitive-game modulus controls values and certified rules, while the nonstandard two-sided experiment-equivalence premise, separate almost-sure legality and numerical boundedness, and joint total-variation premise control every bounded endpoint loss; multiplicity and active-face changes therefore do not invalidate the conditional feasible transfer.
statements.gap: Theorem 3 of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local gives the feasible fully differentiable rule, while Assumption 5 and Theorem 5 give feasible transfer for its directionally differentiable centrosymmetric rule. HiranoPorter2009 motivates pointwise limit-experiment treatment-rule analysis but does not supply the compact-\(H\), two-sided total-variation equivalence or the joint approximation with an estimated game assumed here. The present theorem conditionally treats the non-centrosymmetric polyhedral class and quantifies perturbation error uniformly over saddle and indexability ties; FangSantos2019 and FirpoGalvaoParker2023 explain why pointwise plug-in reasoning alone is insufficient at such nonsmooth boundaries.
statements.consumer: Researchers estimating covariance and bound derivatives obtain a feasible treatment rule whose regret guarantee remains valid near face and indexability boundaries.

sampling_model.design: The canonical experiment is one observation \(Z_h\sim N(h,\Sigma)\). Transfer from \(P_{n,h}\) is conditional on the nonstandard uniform two-sided experiment-equivalence premise, not on ordinary pointwise local asymptotic normality.
sampling_model.units: The target population is summarized locally by the reduced-form mean \(h\in H\) and the partially identified causal welfare contrast \(U^{\ast}\).
sampling_model.treatment: The rule \(\delta(Z_h)\in[0,1]\) is the fraction or probability assigned to treatment; both deterministic and randomized measurable rules are allowed.
sampling_model.overlap: No propensity-score overlap condition is imposed in the Gaussian endpoint game; feasibility is the nonempty interval \([\ell(h),u(h)]\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For transfer, \(\widehat Z_n\) is generated by the forward kernel \(K_n\) from the nonstandard two-sided experiment-equivalence premise. A sufficient construction on the standard Borel space \(\mathcal X_n\) uses a measurable statistic \(T_n\) with a uniform Gaussian-pivot error \(a_n\to0\) and an \(h\)-independent reconstruction kernel \(\mathsf R_n\) with uniform reconstruction error \(b_n\to0\); setting \(K_n(x,\cdot)=\delta_{T_n(x)}\) and \(L_n=\mathsf R_n\) gives \(\lambda_n\le a_n+b_n\). A training split constructs \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\), including \(\widehat\Sigma_n\), and is required separately to return a member of \(\mathcal G_p\) satisfying \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}\), \(P_{n,h}\)-almost surely for every \(n\) and \(h\in H\); the numerical bounds alone do not imply legal membership. A conditionally independent evaluation split constructs \(\widehat Z_n\), and uniform convergence to zero of the expected conditional total-variation distance from \(N(h,\widehat\Sigma_n)\) implies \(\gamma_n\to0\). The reference \(Q_{n,h}\) has exactly the same \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\)-marginal as \(P_{n,h}\), so legality and the numerical bounds hold under both joint laws before the certified selector is run. Primitive error is then measured by \(\alpha_n\), and the decision is computed to certified gap \(\varepsilon_n\). No rate for \(a_n\), \(b_n\), or \(\lambda_n\) is asserted.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Assumption 5(i) imposes convexity and centrosymmetry, Theorem 4 supplies selected rules for that directionally differentiable Gaussian limit game, Theorem 5 gives its feasible transfer, and the Conclusion leaves the joint directional-differentiability and non-centrosymmetry regime open.
Theorem 1 gives a minimax-regret rule and exact value over all decision rules for a Gaussian experiment with a convex centrosymmetric parameter space by using a modulus extremizer.

Definition 2 imposes sign ambiguity on an open set, and Theorem 3 proves infinitely many minimax-regret rules in a centrosymmetric class and excludes linear threshold rules under additional conditions, without characterizing every unrestricted optimum.
Theorem 1 returns an epsilon-minimax mixture after finitely many Hedge iterations when the statistician mixes over a fixed finite menu of rules.
The paper derives exact asymmetric-regret treatment rules for point-identified experiments with threshold structure.
The paper shows that ordinary bootstrap consistency for directionally differentiable functionals generally requires full differentiability and develops derivative-aware inference.

tldr: Sampling uncertainty and partial identification produce a Gaussian endpoint game whose exact solution is known for fully differentiable bounds without centrosymmetry and for directionally differentiable bounds under centrosymmetry, but not in the orthogonal regime combining polyhedral kinks with asymmetry. Under a weaker pointwise sign-ambiguity condition, the core reduces Nature to signed endpoint states, characterizes every saddle over the weak-star compact \(L^{\infty}\) class of measurable randomized rules, constructs a face-complete least-favorable prior by finitely averaging face-specific optima, and supplies convergent exchange certificates. A triangular game proves that the actual two-dimensional compact-polyhedral overlap with the published centrosymmetric result is a proper subclass of \(\mathcal G_2\); it has value \(2/3\) and simultaneous constant one-index and tanh-perturbed non-one-index optima. The principal open objects are a finite normal-fan criterion for the full optimal correspondence and a finite rational unbalanced prior with an exact interval-arithmetic saddle and curvature certificate. On an explicitly bounded primitive collection, an explicit modulus controls risk and value perturbations. Feasible transfer is conditional on a nonstandard compact-\(H\), two-sided total-variation equivalence, for which uniform Gaussian-pivot approximation plus uniform asymptotic reconstruction is a concrete sufficient construction; it also separately requires a legal and numerically bounded estimated game and a joint total-variation condition. Ordinary DQM or pointwise LAN does not supply the two-sided premise, and no transfer-error rate is asserted.

project_justification.gap: Theorem 3 of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local is the feasible fully differentiable result. Its Assumption 5(i) imposes convexity and centrosymmetry for directionally differentiable bounds, Theorem 4 supplies selected rules for that limit game, Theorem 5 gives their feasible transfer, and the Conclusion leaves the joint directional-differentiability and non-centrosymmetry regime open. Yata2025Optimal relies on an antipodal modulus pair. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision imposes open-set sign ambiguity and establishes multiplicity without classifying the full unrestricted correspondence; the present primitive class instead uses a weaker pointwise sign-ambiguity condition.
project_justification.niche: Compact polyhedral endpoint games retain enough finite face geometry for separation and normal-fan analysis, while unrestricted measurable rules retain the economically relevant randomization and perturbation phenomena that disappear under a threshold restriction.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact primal-dual game in the asymmetric compact-polyhedral regime under a pointwise sign-ambiguity condition, characterizes every saddle through Gaussian-mixture Bayes scores and equalizer conditions, constructs a face-complete dual representative by a finite convex combination, and supplies weak-star convergent certificates. It proves the strict inclusion \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\subsetneq\mathcal G_2\) relative to the actual compact-polyhedral Theorem 4 overlap, retains the answer-open geometric indexability criterion and a fully specified rational interval-certificate route for the no-index branch, and gives an explicit bounded-class modulus plus a conditional joint total-variation risk-transfer bound. The feasible clause assumes a nonstandard uniform two-sided experiment equivalence, with uniform Gaussian-pivot approximation and uniform asymptotic reconstruction as a sufficient construction, and invokes the selector only after separate almost-sure premises establish both legal membership of \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\) in \(\mathcal G_p\) and its numerical \(\kappa\)-bounds under the original and reference joint laws.

related_work: Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye, \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local}, Section 4.1, Theorem 3, Section 4.2, Assumption 5 and Theorems 4--5, and the Conclusion, give the feasible fully differentiable rule, impose convexity and centrosymmetry for the directionally differentiable problem, supply selected rules for that limit game, transfer them feasibly, and explicitly leave the joint directional-differentiability and non-centrosymmetry regime open. The compact asymmetric polyhedral class studied here is an orthogonal regime, not a superclass of the paper's full Assumption-5 class. The definition of \(\mathcal O_p^{(4)}\) records the exact compact-polyhedral overlap and makes equality of the two objectives there a sanity check rather than a theorem contribution. The centrosymmetric-overlap proposition proves the non-definitional strict separation \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\subsetneq\mathcal G_2\) using the asymmetric triangular witness. Yata, \cite{Yata2025Optimal}, Introduction, Remark 3, Lemma 3, Theorem 1, and its proof, converts a modulus extremizer into an antipodal least-favorable subproblem and an optimal one-index rule; the centered antipodal clause of the centrosymmetric-overlap proposition derives that rule from the all-saddle conditions, while Remark 3 identifies non-centrosymmetric hardest subfamilies as the first changed proof step. Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye, \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision}, Definition 2, Theorem 3, and its five-step proof, impose sign ambiguity on an open set and use bounded completeness, linear embedding, and binding-risk-preserving perturbations to establish multiplicity. The pointwise sign-ambiguity condition used here is weaker, and that paper does not characterize every optimum or exclude all randomized one-index rules. Tetenov, \cite{Tetenov2012Asymmetric}, supplies the point-identified asymmetric-regret threshold benchmark; the no-index question therefore requires finite rational game and prior data, exact primal-dual closure, and interval enclosures of a curved Gaussian-mixture boundary. Aradillas Fernández et al., \cite{AradillasFernandezEtAl2025Epsilon}, Introduction, Theorem 1, and Conclusion, obtain certified Hedge iterates only over a fixed prespecified rule menu; \cite{AradillasFernandezEtAl2025LeastFavorable}, Sections 2--3 and the duality appendix, supplies the weighted-density Bayes-response architecture for approximate least-favorable distributions. Zhang, Wu, and López, \cite{ZhangWuLopez2010Exchange}, provide the compact semi-infinite exchange template adapted here after the measurable-rule Bayes envelope removes the infinite-dimensional primal minimization. Hirano and Porter, \cite{HiranoPorter2009}, motivate pointwise limit-experiment analysis of treatment rules; they do not establish the compact-\(H\), two-sided total-variation equivalence assumed here, and ordinary DQM or pointwise LAN does not imply it. The explicit sufficient construction instead combines uniform Gaussian-pivot approximation with uniform asymptotic sufficiency and reconstruction on standard Borel sample spaces. The separate joint condition for the statistic and estimated game is justified by a conditional Gaussian approximation under sample splitting or an equivalent stable construction. The feasible transfer additionally imposes legal membership of the estimated game and numerical boundedness as distinct almost-sure premises; preservation of the estimated-game marginal under \(Q_{n,h}\) transports both premises to the reference law before selection. Fang and Santos, \cite{FangSantos2019}, and Firpo, Galvao, and Parker, \cite{FirpoGalvaoParker2023}, provide the directional and marginal-optimization warnings that motivate a tie-uniform near-saddle selector rather than a discontinuous exact optimizer.
technical_internal_limitation: Face completeness is defined relative to face relative interiors that receive positive mass under at least one dual optimum; it does not assert that every geometrically active affine piece must receive least-favorable mass. The convergent certificate uses exact restricted-game and worst-state oracles and deliberately makes no complexity-rate claim. The explicit continuity modulus is uniform only over the stated \(\kappa\)-bounded primitive collection. Feasible transfer requires the nonstandard compact-\(H\), two-sided total-variation experiment equivalence in \(\mathrm{ass:uniform-two-sided-experiment-equivalence}\); neither DQM, pointwise LAN, nor \cite{HiranoPorter2009} supplies this premise. The uniform Gaussian-pivot and asymptotic-reconstruction construction is sufficient, not asserted for every regular model, and \(\lambda_n\) has no claimed rate. Transfer also requires \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\in\mathcal G_p\) and \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)\) almost surely as separate premises; coefficient, face-count, and covariance bounds do not themselves establish legal game-class membership. The novel joint total-variation condition \(\gamma_n\to0\) must be independently verified by the stated conditional Gaussian sample-splitting route or an equivalent stable joint construction. The verified \(2/3\) witness establishes coexistence, not the no-one-index branch; the finite rational unbalanced-prior branch with exact saddle and curvature certificates remains an explicit early kill test.
honest_scope: The settled target is the compact polyhedral Gaussian limit game under pointwise sign ambiguity and its risk transfer conditional on an explicit nonstandard uniform two-sided total-variation equivalence, separate almost-sure legality and \(\kappa\)-boundedness conditions for the estimated game, a novel joint total-variation approximation for the statistic and estimated game, and uniform expected primitive-game error. Ordinary DQM or pointwise LAN does not imply the experiment-equivalence premise. On standard Borel sample spaces, uniform Gaussian-pivot approximation through \(T_n\) and uniform asymptotic sufficiency through the reconstruction kernel \(\mathsf R_n\) provide a sufficient route with \(K_n(x,\cdot)=\delta_{T_n(x)}\), \(L_n=\mathsf R_n\), and \(\lambda_n\le a_n+b_n\to0\); no rate is asserted. The transfer theorem applies the certified selector only on the common full-probability legal event under \(P_{n,h}\) and \(Q_{n,h}\); the latter conclusion uses equality of their estimated-game marginals. Numerical primitive bounds are not treated as establishing membership in \(\mathcal G_p\). As a sanity check, for every \(\mathsf G=(H,\Sigma,\ell,u)\in\mathcal O_p^{(4)}\), substituting the Gaussian mean domain, covariance, and directional-derivative endpoint maps of Theorem 4 of Montiel Olea--Qiu--Stoye makes the two minimax objectives identical by the definition of \(\mathcal O_p^{(4)}\); this identity is not counted as a theorem contribution. The centered antipodal case recovers Yata, and the centrosymmetric-overlap proposition proves only the strict inclusion \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\subsetneq\mathcal G_2\); no containment relation with the paper's full Assumption-5 class is claimed. The rule class is the weak-star compact positive order interval in the \(L^{\infty}\) unit ball, and selector limits are understood in \(\sigma(L^{\infty},L^1)\) on Lebesgue-almost-everywhere classes. Noncompact mean domains, unknown Gaussian covariance without consistent estimation, multiple actions, and semiparametric endpoint maps outside a uniform finite-face approximation are outside scope. The non-tautological indexability criterion and the finite rational unbalanced no-index construction with an exact interval-arithmetic saddle and curvature certificate are deliberately open-ended questions.

novelty_justification: The closest paper, MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local, uses Theorem 3 for the feasible fully differentiable rule, then imposes convexity and centrosymmetry in Assumption 5(i), supplies selected rules for the directionally differentiable limit game in Theorem 4, and transfers them feasibly in Theorem 5. Its Conclusion leaves the joint directional-differentiability and non-centrosymmetry regime open. The compact asymmetric polyhedral class here occupies that orthogonal regime but is not asserted to contain the paper's full Assumption-5 class. The proposed dual lets Nature range over signed endpoint priors and characterizes every saddle in a weak-star compact \(L^{\infty}\) rule space; a finite convex combination of face-specific optimal priors gives a face-complete representative under the relative-interior definition. The triangular construction proves the strict inclusion \(\mathcal O_2^{(4)}\subsetneq\mathcal G_2\) relative to the actual compact-polyhedral Theorem 4 overlap and exhibits value \(2/3\) with one-index and non-one-index optima. Equality of objectives on \(\mathcal O_p^{(4)}\) is retained only as a definitional sanity check. The pointwise sign-ambiguity condition is weaker than Definition 2 of MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision and is not attributed to that source. Yata2025Optimal supplies the antipodal centered benchmark. The transfer contribution is limited to an explicit modulus on a \(\kappa\)-bounded primitive collection and the display \(-M_{\kappa}\lambda_n\le\mathcal R_n^{\mathrm{loc}}(\widehat\delta_n)-v\le\varepsilon_n+2\alpha_n+M_{\kappa}\gamma_n\). Its feasible clause is conditional on the nonstandard compact-\(H\), two-sided total-variation equivalence in \(\mathrm{ass:uniform-two-sided-experiment-equivalence}\); DQM, pointwise LAN, and \cite{HiranoPorter2009} do not supply that premise. On standard Borel sample spaces, uniform Gaussian-pivot approximation and uniform asymptotic sufficiency through an \(h\)-independent reconstruction kernel give the stated sufficient construction with \(\lambda_n\le a_n+b_n\to0\), without a manufactured rate or a claim covering every regular model. The feasible clause separately assumes that \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\) is a legal member of \(\mathcal G_p\) and satisfies the numerical predicate \(\mathsf B_{\kappa}\), \(P_{n,h}\)-almost surely for every \(n\) and \(h\); the common estimated-game marginal transports both properties to \(Q_{n,h}\) before selection and before \(\alpha_n\) is invoked. Conditional Gaussian approximation under sample splitting gives a concrete sufficient route to \(\gamma_n\to0\); it does not establish legality, and numerical bounds do not encode it. The algebraic gap inequality is isolated as a lemma. These are field-tier decision-theory results without a manufactured lower bound. The remaining indexability result is honestly open and is constrained to a finite primitive-geometry certificate, while the no-index kill test requires a finite rational prior, exact primal-dual equality, and an explicit interval-arithmetic curvature certificate.
message: Retagged the transfer premise as nonstandard uniform two-sided experiment equivalence, added the explicit Gaussian-pivot and reconstruction construction, preserved the conditional regret bound, synchronized all transfer caveats, and passed the proposal gate.
